exercises: notes on a schema node reached through a $ref, against the inline case as a control, on both a parameter and a property
note:
This isolates a contract detail that is easy to state approximately and wrong to leave that way.

A note on a parameter's schema renders when that schema is written inline. That is the convention a real corpus uses and it works. A note on a schema reached through a reference does not render, because the row reads notes from the node as written while reading the description from the node the reference resolves to. The description and the note sit on the same object and only one of them arrives.

Both rows here carry both a description and a note on the referenced schema, so the asymmetry is visible side by side: if REFERENCED DESCRIPTION appears and REFERENCED NOTE does not, that is the defect, and the inline rows above and below prove the note mechanism itself is working.
